Yeah im curious about the work on those greaves too. You see it a lot on bronze armor. Is it cast on a mold created from the warriors own body?

For the helmets and cuirasses, they would have been shaped on a mold (they were custom made to fit the warrior). I can't really find anything detailing the exact process used for each piece of armour, other than material + template + hammering = item. I'm not sure how they made the molds the pieces were shaped on.

But from what I can gather, the bronze greaves were indeed finished while being worn. The greaves were made of a thinner, flexible sheet of bronze (rather than the heavy plate used in helmets and cuirasses), and "sprung on" to the warriors leg, with a soft backing for comfort, fixed in place with an ankle ring and often had straps (the shape and elasticity of the sheets meant they could possibly be worn without fastening straps, if they desired)

I assume the sheets were measured and cut to the appropriate length, were crudely shaped on an anvil or mold, fitted, then finished as they were being worn to fit the shape of the warriors leg perfectly. Additional adornments, such as engravings and other ornate detailing were likely added afterwards by the smith to personalise the piece.
